gemini.partial_finding: High / Approach - contradiction in how the shared/ tree is checked: the spec says 'replace both sentinels with a delivered-file-set comparison' but the mini-plan retains _shared_healthy as the gate. If the main gate keeps using the sentinel for shared, a partial shared/ reap still short-circuits and remains unfixed (the exact ADR-120 failure ...[truncated]

findings.finding: delivered(src) - delivered(dst) only detects absent paths, but the plan claims it also repairs truncated files. A truncated destination file is still present, so no overlay copy is triggered.
findings.resolution: Accepted; scoped out with evidence. Probed the live cache: comparing sizes between the marketplace clone and cached shared/ reports 24 of 1015 files differing (scripts/lib/__init__.py 29 vs 28 - one CRLF byte). A content rule here would re-copy them every session. Truncation detection belongs to check_plugin_cache_sync.py, which CRLF-normalizes before hashing. Claim removed from the spec; limitation stated explicitly and carried as ledger row 23.

findings.finding: The walk must be copytree-equivalent: _IGNORE called at every source directory, ignored directory names pruned before recursion. A generic rglob() descends into .in_use before excluding it.
findings.resolution: Accepted. _delivered() is an explicit top-down stack traversal calling _IGNORE(str(current), names) on each directory's own child names and pruning directories before descent. Pinned by test_delivered_prunes_ignored_dirs_without_descending.

findings.finding: Swallowing OSError per-dir can turn an incomplete scan into a false healthy result; an under-counted source hides missing destination files.
findings.resolution: Accepted. _delivered() returns None (never a short set) on any enumeration failure; _incomplete() propagates it. Both call sites use identity comparisons (is True / is not True), so unknown neither claims health nor copies.

findings.finding: The early no-op condition must use shared completeness, not _shared_healthy; otherwise a surviving shared sentinel can still suppress the new check.
findings.resolution: Accepted. The combined early return is deleted; _plugins_healthy is removed entirely and _heal_plugins is called unconditionally (self-no-op'ing). Pinned by test_neither_short_circuit_survives, which leaves BOTH sentinels alive with a different non-sentinel file missing from each tree.

findings.finding: Path existence alone is insufficient when the destination has the wrong entry type (a directory where a file belongs, a broken symlink).
findings.resolution: Accepted, and free. Both sides are built by the same file-only walk and compared as sets, so a directory or broken symlink at a file's path is simply absent from the destination set and counts as a gap. No exists() call remains in the code. Pinned by test_incomplete_true_when_a_directory_stands_where_a_file_belongs.

findings.finding: The new always-run tree walker expands routine interaction with marketplace/cache content, including possible links; keep traversal and relative-path construction rooted.
findings.resolution: Accepted. Paths are always derived via relative_to(root); non-file entries are never recorded. Symlinked directories ARE followed, matching copytree(symlinks=False), which is the behaviour being mirrored.

openai.overall: Delivered-file-set comparison is the right direction and the shared-tree expansion is justified, but the implementation needs a precise copytree-equivalent walker and a decision on whether 'partial' includes truncated/type-corrupted files.

note: All six findings were resolved BEFORE implementation. The resolutions table lives in the iterate spec; the Stage-1 spec-reviewer independently verified GPT-2/3/5 against the code.
